research.abstract: Background. Economic inactivity due to ill-health has been rising in the United Kingdom. Chronic health conditions make up most of the burden of poor health, and frequently co-occur, yet the impact of multimorbidity on economic inactivity remains underexplored. Methods. Data was from three British birth cohorts (born in 1946, 1958 and 1970). Psychological distress, chronic back pain and cardiometabolic disease were assessed in participants' thirties and forties, and economic inactivity one to two decades later. Modified Poisson regression models with robust standard errors estimated associations between health and inactivity, accounting for economic activity at baseline and several socioeconomic and demographic confounders. We tested for multiplicative and additive interaction between condition pairs. Results. The prevalence of all three health conditions increased with age. Each was associated with a higher risk of later economic inactivity in fully adjusted models. Psychological distress was the strongest and most consistent predictor across cohorts (RR = 1.22 (95% CI 0.90-1.64) to 1.99 (95% CI 1.67-2.38)). Comorbidity was common; more than 10% of participants experienced two or more conditions in their forties. Risk of economic inactivity increased with multimorbidity. However, we found little evidence that risk for comorbidity exceeded the sum of individual conditions on either the multiplicative or additive scales. Conclusions. Common chronic conditions in adulthood, particularly when comorbid, are associated with a substantially higher risk of economic inactivity across decades-long time horizons. This association has persisted over time and across policy contexts.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Salmonella Typhimurium is a versatile foodborne pathogen with a broad ecological range, making it an ideal model to better understand pathogen adaptations that allow them to infect multiple hosts and persist across environments. Here, we analysed 595 genomes of S. Typhimurium representing three food animal sources (bovine, swine, and poultry) and one non‐food animal source (wild birds). We found that S. Typhimurium from food animal sources generally had a more open pangenome and harboured more antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). Notably, swine isolates exhibited the most open pangenome and the highest prevalence of ARGs, patterns that were associated with a greater presence of mobile genetic elements, particularly plasmids. Despite similar core genome sizes, S. Typhimurium from different sources displayed distinct patterns of positive selection in the core genome that varied in frequency and targeted functional categories. In contrast, although accessory genome sizes varied substantially across sources, the frequency of positive selection remained similar. Using machine learning, we identified source‐predictive genetic variants, many of which are associated with stress‐response functions. These findings suggest that gain and loss of accessory genes and positive selection acting on core genes support differential adaptation in S. Typhimurium, potentially contributing to its broad ecological range.

research.abstract: Environmental chemical exposures may influence biological aging, but their relationships with epigenetic aging and related health outcomes remain incompletely understood. In this study, we evaluated the associations of 13 environmental exposures, including heavy metals, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), and volatile organic compounds (VOCs), with epigenetic aging in 666 older adults from the Forensic Research via Omics Markers in Environmental Health Vulnerable Areas (FROM) cohort. Among the evaluated epigenetic aging biomarkers, GrimAge acceleration showed the most prominent associations, with 2-hydroxyfluorene (2-HF), 2-naphthol (2-NAP), blood cadmium (bCd), and methylhippuric acid (MHA) exhibiting significant positive associations (strongest for 2-HF: beta = 0.491 years per doubling of exposure, P = 1.22 x 10-14). Quantile g-computation showed that combined environmental exposures were significantly associated with increased GrimAge acceleration (psi = 0.497, 95% CI: 0.013-0.981, P = 0.044), and Bayesian kernel machine regression identified 2-HF and 2-NAP as major contributors. Among clinical traits, white blood cell count (WBC) and gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) were significantly and positively associated with GrimAge acceleration, and two-sample Mendelian randomization provided nominal support for a positive effect of GrimAge acceleration on GGT. Mediation analyses identified significant indirect effects through GrimAge acceleration for the associations of 2-HF, 2-NAP, bCd, and MHA with GGT. Exploratory disease analyses further suggested potential associations with diabetic nephropathy and osteoporosis, together with an inverse association with cardiac valvular disease. These findings suggest that environmental chemical exposures are associated with accelerated epigenetic aging, which may represent a biological pathway linking environmental exposures to metabolic and age-related health outcomes.

research.abstract: Background Diabetic retinopathy is a leading cause of preventable blindness. Because it is asymptomatic until substantial damage has occurred, periodic retinal examination is essential for early detection. Evidence on uptake where eye services are co-located with diabetes care in Ethiopia is lacking. This study assessed the prevalence of, and factors associated with, adequate diabetic retinopathy screening practice among adults with diabetes attending Menelik II Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Addis Ababa. Methods We conducted an institution-based cross-sectional study from December 2023 to February 2024 among adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes on follow-up for at least three months, selected by systematic random sampling and interviewed with a structured questionnaire. Knowledge and attitude were classified using a modified Bloom's cut-off of 80%, and screening practice as adequate when at least two of three recommended practices were met. Factors associated with adequate practice were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Results Of 404 patients approached, 371 were interviewed and included in the analysis (response rate 91.8%). Adequate screening practice was found in 139 participants (37.5%, 95% confidence interval [CI] 32.7-42.5); 62.0% had adequate knowledge and 72.8% a favorable attitude. Adequate practice was associated with adequate knowledge (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 5.10, 95% CI 2.81-9.25), a known eye disorder (AOR 3.96, 95% CI 2.11-7.43), higher education (AOR 3.82, 95% CI 1.33-10.95), age 41-65 years (AOR 3.15, 95% CI 1.10-9.03) and being married (AOR 1.73, 95% CI 1.01-2.97). Cost, lack of time and travel distance were the most commonly reported barriers. Conclusion Fewer than four in ten adults with diabetes underwent retinal examination at the recommended frequency despite on-site specialist eye care. The strong association with existing eye disorders suggests that examination is often prompted by ocular problems rather than undertaken for prevention. Strengthening patient education during diabetes follow-up and a direct referral pathway to on-site eye services may improve uptake.

research.abstract: Estimating the effective sample size (ESS) is fundamental in Bayesian phylogenetic inference to account for autocorrelation in MCMC samples. While methods for continuous parameters are well established, the discrete and high-dimensional nature of treespace poses substantial challenges. In this paper, we introduce a new approach based on Conditional Clade Distributions (CCDs) to emulate MCMC chains with known ESS bounds. We compare existing tree ESS estimators with novel approaches that utilize CCDs as tractable tree distributions, as well as a new probabilistic estimator based on differences in clade frequencies between independent chains. Using our emulated chains from both simulated and real datasets, we assess estimators for their ability to recover the true ESS (accuracy), their insensitivity to the removal of autocorrelated samples from the chain (stability), and their tolerance to combining multiple chains together (robustness). We further examine how multimodality and poor inter-mode chain mixing can compromise the reliability of tree ESS estimates. These findings indicate that our new CCD-based estimators perform comparably to existing approaches with respect to accuracy, stability, and robustness. In contrast, the probabilistic estimator and two previously recommended methods incur prohibitive computational costs for long chains. Together, these results establish a new framework for evaluating tree ESS estimators using CCD-based emulated MCMC chains and demonstrate their performance and current limitations in practical phylogenetic analyses. The expanded suite of tree ESS estimators is available in the user-friendly TreeStat2 software package for BEAST 2.

research.abstract: PREPRINT-25 (v1.0.0 Empirical Preprint) • 100% Native Rust bio-suite-supervisor Across 544 Verified NCBI Records (L = 52,227 Aligned Columns) We reconstruct the Paleozoic-to-Anthropocene phylogenomic radiation, kleptocnidae/chemosensory/terpenoid enzyme evolution, and multi-compartment marine demographic history of the global radiation of Nudibranchia and allied Nudipleura (spanning Suborder Cladobranchia [Berghia stephanieae, Spurilla braziliana, Hermissenda emurai, Facelina bostoniensis, Phestilla fuscostriata, Tritonia tetraquetra, Melibe leonina, Dendronotus frondosus, Doto coronata, Dermatobranchus otome] and Suborder Doridina [Hexabranchus sanguineus, Polycera hedgpethi, Nembrotha kubaryana, Doris pseudoargus, Peltodoris atromaculata, Dendrodoris krusensternii, Phyllidia elegans, Phyllidiella pustulosa, Cadlina japonica, Chromodoris annae, C. lochi, Goniobranchus leopardus, Doriprismatica atromarginata, Glossodoris acosti, Hypselodoris whitei], rooted on Pleurobranchida and Tectipleura outgroups Aplysia californica and Elysia chlorotica) across 544 active verified NCBI sequence records (plus 6 autonomously quarantined GenBank UNVERIFIED anomalies) comprising a 64-taxon, 18-locus supermatrix (L = 52,227 aligned columns), 48 nuclear functional coding sequences, and 12 regional and multi-locus cohorts (12 x N = 36 = 432 isolates). Executed end-to-end via autonomous Native Rust bio-suite-supervisor optimization across 32 candidate RuNIE chains (total runtime 236.53 s; B = 1,000 UFBoot; 25,000 MCMC generations with 20% burn-in), RY3 purine/pyrimidine recoding under GTR+F+R4 reduces heterobranch compositional heterogeneity by 85.8% (RCFV = 0.0052 vs. 0.0365, ln L = -600,241.59), dating Root Heterobranchia to 284.6 Ma, Crown Nudipleura to 236.4 Ma, Crown Nudibranchia (Cladobranchia vs. Doridina) to 198.2 Ma, and Crown Chromodoridoidea to 52.8 Ma. Native Rust quartet multispecies coalescent inference (runie-quartet-coalescent across 18 gene trees and 11,436,768 quartets in 43.90 ms) recovers 8,586,986 satisfied quartets (normalized Q = 0.7508, mean LPP = 0.8864) while ABBA-BABA tests quantify reticulate allele sharing across Indo-Pacific Chromodoris/Goniobranchus mimicry rings and Phyllidiidae spongivores. Sixty-one-state Goldman-Yang codon models identify strong purifying constraint on cnidosac C-type lectin/cathepsin cores (omega_0 = 0.000) and Hsp70/BiP/DnaJ heatwave chaperones alongside 4D Bayes Empirical Bayes diversifying selection on rhinophore nAChR/mGluR/Kv receptors (peak BEB omega = 7.12) and CYP3A29/CYP4F1 terpenoid-sequestering monooxygenase pockets (foreground omega_fg = 0.001, peak BEB omega = 2.75). Finally, 12 coupled Bayesian coalescent skylines contrast Last Glacial Maximum shelf-exposure bottlenecks, Holocene Coral Triangle lagoon expansions, and pelagic Glaucus gyre stability against sharp locus-specific Ne compressions at nuclear Histone H3 / terpenoid-linked loci relative to neutral mitochondrial COX1 (1Ne) and Katoh E-INS-i-aligned ribosomal 16S/28S rDNA (4Ne) reservoirs. Autonomous 100% Native Rust bio-suite-supervisor synthesis across 544 verified NCBI records (L = 52,227 aligned columns, 32 RuNIE chains, 11.44M quartets, 300k MCMC generations in 236.53 s) resolves the 284.6 Ma-to-present global radiation, kleptocnidae & CYP3A29 terpenoid evolution, and 12 regional vs. multi-locus skylines of Nudibranchia. research.abstract: 32-chain RuNIE phylogenomic and functional selection analysis across 64 species and 16 loci (L = 37,741 aligned columns; Carabidae, Scarabaeidae, Coccinellidae, Cerambycidae, Chrysomelidae, and Curculionidae) coupled with 10,000-generation (20% burn-in) Bayesian coalescent skyline reconstructions across three independent PopSets (Dendroctonus ponderosae, Harmonia axyridis, and Pterostichus melanarius) benchmarked against *MAFFT, *IQ-TREE/*LSD2, *PAML codeml, and *BEAST v1.10.4 The hyperdiverse radiation of beetles (Order Coleoptera) across terrestrial ecosystems was propelled by key physiological and enzymatic innovations—from cursorial predation and pygidial chemical defense in Adephaga (Carabidae) and hindgut microbial fermentation in Scarabaeiformia (Scarabaeidae) to cryptonephridic Malpighian tubule water conservation in Cucujiformia (Coccinellidae) and horizontally transferred plant cell wall degrading enzymes (GH5, GH28, and GH45) in Phytophaga (Cerambycidae, Chrysomelidae, and Curculionidae). Here we execute a 32-chain RuNIE phylogenomic and functional selection analysis across a 16-locus, 64-species supermatrix (L = 37,741 aligned columns with 15,440 parsimony-informative sites) coupled with independent 10,000-generation (20% burn-in) Bayesian coalescent skyline reconstructions across three localized population datasets benchmarking Native Rust against *MAFFT, *IQ-TREE with *LSD2, *PAML codeml, and *BEAST. Our dated chronogram and codon selection models anchor Crown Coleoptera at 295.0 Ma, Cucujiformia cryptonephridic water conservation at 224.8 Ma, and the Phytophaga cell-wall enzyme radiation at 174.0 Ma, revealing strong purifying constraint on GH28 pectinases (omega = 0.2251) alongside diversifying selection on CYP6 detoxification monooxygenases (omega = 1.0657). Across the three localized PopSet skyline cohorts, we resolve an 11.1-fold Anthropocene drought and winter-warming outbreak expansion in the mountain pine beetle Dendroctonus ponderosae (Ne = 184,439 to 2,052,657), an 88.1% biocontrol founder bottleneck followed by a 37.4-fold invasive bridgehead explosion in Harmonia axyridis (Ne = 62,937 to 2,351,789), and an 83.0% agrochemical intensification crash followed by beetle-bank corridor recovery in the epigean predator Pterostichus melanarius, while demonstrating that *MAFFT progressive alignment consumes 80.1% of external pipeline runtime compared to a 21.0-fold end-to-end speedup in Native Rust. research.abstract: Abstract Phylogenetic analyses of molecular evolution often require repeated manual preparation to reconcile taxa, annotate trees, execute models, and summarize results. These steps become increasingly time-consuming and difficult to standardize as the number of taxa, genes, and analytical hypotheses increases. We present HYphlow, an open-source graphical workflow developed in Python that integrates data preparation, trait-based foreground branch assignment, HyPhy execution, and structured result extraction within a single interface. HYphlow reconciles taxon labels across alignments, trees, and trait data; reconstructs ancestral states using parsimony and maximum likelihood; generates alternative foreground annotations; executes HyPhy analyses locally or through portable scripts for high-performance computing; and records analytical decisions and settings throughout the workflow. We evaluated HYphlow using simulations and two published datasets comprising cryptochrome analyses in pigeons and doves and visual opsin analyses in skinks. A name-similarity threshold of 80 reliably recovered simulated spelling variants, while consensus foreground assignment increased precision relative to parsimony or maximum likelihood alone (0.928 vs 0.891 and 0.907, respectively), with a corresponding reduction in recall (0.875 vs 0.921 and 0.918). In the empirical datasets, HYphlow reconciled taxon labels, reconstructed or reproduced foreground hypotheses derived using different approaches, and generated selection results consistent with the principal conclusions of the original studies. HYphlow therefore provides a reproducible framework for carrying comparative molecular evolutionary analyses from independently prepared sequence, phylogenetic, and trait data through branch assignment, model execution, and results summary while retaining researcher control over analytical decisions. HYphlow is freely available under the MIT licence from GitHub at: https://github.com/Schott-Lab/HYphlow .

research.abstract: Abstract Borrelia burgdorferi , the causative agent of Lyme borreliosis, persists in mammalian hosts despite robust activation of innate and adaptive immunity. A hallmark of murine infection is the production of low-avidity antibodies, yet the immunological mechanisms underlying this defective humoral response remain poorly understood. Here, we used single-cell RNA sequencing of draining lymph node cells from Borrelia-infected mice at days 7 and 14 post-infection, comparing transcriptional profiles with those from mice immunised with heat-killed Borrelia or with a potent germinal centre-inducing protein immunisation. Borrelia infection induced a rapid germinal centre response, however, light zone B cells displayed diminished expression of co-stimulatory and T-B cell interaction molecules while maintaining core germinal centre identity markers, suggesting impaired positive selection. T follicular helper cells upregulated multiple inhibitory checkpoint receptor genes, most prominently Ctla4, alongside an active germinal centre engagement programme. Foxp3⁺ regulatory T cells upregulated genes associated with follicular-homing and suppressive function, including those implicated in CTLA-4-mediated trans-endocytosis. To test whether inhibitory signalling contributes to the impaired humoral response, infected mice were treated with anti-CTLA-4 blocking antibody. CTLA-4 blockade significantly increased plasma cell numbers and enhanced both the magnitude and avidity of Borrelia - specific IgG responses, including the induction of complement-fixing IgG2a. These findings reveal that CTLA-4-dependent inhibitory signalling contributes to defective antibody quality during Borrelia infection, identifying a mechanism by which dysregulated T cell responses may facilitate impaired humoral control of a persistent spirochaetal pathogen. Authors summary Borrelia burgdorferi , the bacteria that cause Lyme borreliosis, can persist in the body for long periods despite triggering a strong immune response. One puzzling feature of this infection is that the antibodies produced are often of poor quality and do not bind the bacteria effectively. To investigate why, we examined individual immune cells in lymph nodes of Borrelia -infected mice and compared them with cells from mice that received non-living Borrelia or a vaccine- like immunisation known to generate strong antibody responses. Although Borrelia infection rapidly triggered the formation of structures that normally help the immune system refine and improve antibodies, key communication signals between immune cells were reduced. At the same time, both helper and regulatory T cells showed increased activity of molecular pathways that act as brakes on immune responses. One such brake, controlled by a molecule called CTLA-4, appeared particularly important. When we blocked CTLA-4 during infection, mice produced more antibody-secreting cells and generated antibodies that had improved functional properties. Our findings identify a mechanism that limits antibody quality during Borrelia infection and help explain how the bacteria can evade effective immune control and persist in the host.

research.abstract: Abstract Diet has been a major selective force throughout human evolution, yet dietary adaptation is often studied through individual loci rather than as interconnected systems of traits. Here, we integrated genome-wide association data for 58 diet-related phenotypes with genomes from 938 ancient Europeans spanning the last 10,000 years to reconstruct the evolution of dietary endophenotypes. We identified four major systems encompassing adiposity and metabolism, body composition, fatty-acid metabolism and food-related behaviours. Multiple endophenotypes showed significant temporal shifts during the Holocene departing from the expected under neutrality, including coordinated decreases in genetic architectures associated with adiposity, insulin regulation and lipid metabolism, alongside increases in traits related to docosahexaenoic acid metabolism. Moreover, these patterns showed marked geographic heterogeneity across Europe. Our results indicate that dietary adaptation proceeded through coordinated evolutionary changes across interconnected physiological systems, providing a systems-level perspective on how cultural and subsistence transitions reshaped human biology.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Chronic inflammation persists in populations with high HIV and tuberculosis (TB) burden, even during suppressive therapy. Tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) is a key mediator, but its correlates beyond infectious status remain unclear in people living with HIV on stable antiretroviral therapy and who are virologically suppressed. We investigated clinical, metabolic, and neurohormonal correlates of TNF-α in a Zambian cohort. Methods This was a cross-sectional study, which included 227 adults recruited from the outpatient medical clinic at Livingstone University Teaching Hospital in the Southern Province of Zambia. Simple and multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to determine independent associations with plasma TNF-α levels. Models were adjusted for HIV serostatus and history of TB. Standardized beta coefficients (β_std) were computed to compare the relative magnitude of associations across predictors measured on different scales. Results Among 227 participants, 64.8% were living with HIV (95.3% on integrase strand transfer inhibitor-based ART) and 14.0% had a history of tuberculosis. In multivariable analysis, the strongest independent associations with TNF-α were observed within the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS): angiotensin II (β = 1.18 per pg/mL, p < 0.001; β_std = 0.51) and aldosterone (β = 0.884 per pg/mL, p < 0.001; β_std = 0.47). Living with HIV serostatus was also independently associated with higher TNF-α (β = 2581.1 pg/mL, p = 0.018; β_std = 0.19), while the history of TB was not. Significant metabolic factors associated with TNF-α levels included VLDL (β = 4397.4 per mmol/L, p = 0.038; β_std = 0.16) and triglycerides (β = 1971.6 per mmol/L, p = 0.034; β_std = 0.17). Inflammatory markers sST2 (β = 104.4 per ng/mL, p < 0.001; β_std = 0.31), IL-17 A (β = 1.137 per pg/mL, p = 0.003; β_std = 0.21), and D-dimer (β = 0.037 per pg/mL, p = 0.001; β_std = 0.22) were independently associated, as was plasma potassium (β = 107.3 per mmol/L, p < 0.001; β_std = 0.46). Renin, IL-6, IL-5, hs-CRP, and left ventricular mass were not associated with TNF-α. Conclusion In this high-burden population, RAAS activation was an independent correlate of TNF-α, exceeding the effect of HIV serostatus. These findings support the hypothesis that RAAS inhibition may have anti-inflammatory effects; however, this remains to be tested in prospective and interventional studies.

research.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bedaquiline (BDQ), pretomanid (Pa) and linezolid (LZD)-based (BPaL) regimens have transformed rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (RR-TB) treatment. However, resistance to these drugs is increasingly reported, while longitudinal data integrating clinical, phenotypic and genomic evolution remain limited. CASE PRESENTATION: We report a fatal case of recurrent RR-TB in a 40-year-old South African woman with HIV infection who received BPaL therapy. Following treatment completion, recurrent disease was complicated by pregnancy, treatment interruption and loss to follow-up. She subsequently re-presented with advanced cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis and respiratory failure. Despite re-initiation of BPaL, she deteriorated and died from septic shock. Routine drug susceptibility testing, available posthumously, confirmed resistance to BDQ, Pa and LZD. Seven sequential Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates collected during treatment underwent minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) testing and whole-genome sequencing. All demonstrated phenotypic resistance to the three BPaL drugs. Serial genomic analysis identified progressive Rv0678 diversification associated with a two-fold increase in BDQ MIC, while resistance-associated rrl and fbiC mutations remained comparatively stable despite persistently elevated LZD and Pa MICs. CONCLUSIONS: This case demonstrates the interaction of treatment interruption, delayed resistance detection and continued within-host bacterial adaptation during BPaL therapy. Longitudinal phenotypic and genomic findings revealed distinct resistance trajectories among BPaL drugs, highlighting the importance of treatment retention, timely susceptibility testing and genomic surveillance for preserving BPaL effectiveness.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Low-coverage plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) sequencing is an inexpensive substrate for cancer detection. Standard pipelines discard fragments with low mapping quality, which originate mostly from repetitive DNA, although pericentromeric satellite repeats are frequently hypomethylated in cancer. We asked whether the fraction of multi-mapping cfDNA fragments differs between early-stage cancer and matched healthy controls, and how it compares with conventional fragmentomic features under strict control of technical factors. Methods We analysed public plasma cfDNA whole-genome sequencing from 25 patients with stage I–III breast cancer and 25 healthy controls matched 1:1 for age, sex, smoking and alcohol use, each pair processed in the same library and sequencing batch, and from 8 early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cases with 8 matched controls. For every sample we computed the fraction of autosomal fragments with MAPQ < 30 and the share of these fragments located in centromeric and heterochromatic cytobands, and related them to stage, grade and copy-number deviation as proxies of tumour burden. Classifiers were evaluated by leave-one-pair-out cross-validation in breast cancer and, trained on breast cancer only, applied unchanged to HCC. Robustness to GC content and sequencing depth was tested by within-fold residualisation and by fragment-level GC weighting. Conventional fragmentomic features (fragment length, end motifs, copy number, DELFI-like profiles and window features at transcription start sites) were evaluated under four GC-handling analyses. Results The multi-mapping fraction was higher in breast cancer than in matched controls (median 5.38 % vs 5.19 %; higher in 19/25 pairs; paired p = 0.0006; cross-validated AUC 0.81, 95 % CI 0.67–0.94), in stage I (9/10 pairs), stage II (7/10) and stage III (3/5) disease and in every sequencing batch. The excess was concentrated in centromeric and heterochromatic bands, whose share of multi-mapping fragments rose from 22.0 % to 23.4 % (19/25 pairs; p = 0.004). Both signals persisted after within-fold adjustment for GC content and/or depth (AUC 0.64–0.76 for the multi-mapping fraction, 0.71–0.76 for the heterochromatic share) and under fragment-level GC weighting (18/25 pairs; p = 0.003). The multi-mapping difference was largest in stage I and decreased with stage (Spearman ρ = −0.42, p = 0.04), and neither feature was associated with grade or copy-number deviation. In public tissue methylomes, satellites were hypomethylated in breast tumours to a similar extent as other late-replicating DNA, but the bin-level association between tumour hypomethylation and the cfDNA excess was weak and was explained by GC content. In HCC, the pre-specified endpoint, the breast-trained multi-mapping model, was not met (AUC 0.73; 5/8 pairs; sign test p = 0.36). In an exploratory analysis that was not pre-specified, the heterochromatic share was higher in 7/8 HCC pairs (p = 0.016; locked AUC 0.86, 95 % CI 0.62–1.00); across all 33 pairs, including the discovery pairs, it was higher in the cancer case in 26 (post hoc sign test p = 0.0007). In contrast, conventional fragmentomic features reached AUC 0.71 (breast) and 0.77 (HCC) only without fragment-level GC control; they tracked the per-sample coverage–GC dependence and fell to chance under each of three GC-controlled analyses, including one that preserves promoter-specific signal. Conclusions Multi-mapping cfDNA fragments, which are routinely discarded, differed between early-stage breast cancer and batch-matched controls, largely independently of GC content and sequencing depth, with an excess in centromeric and heterochromatic DNA. The signal did not scale with stage, its biological origin is unproven, and a read-quality contribution cannot be excluded from fragment files. It is a candidate marker that requires confirmation in larger cohorts with raw reads and tumour-fraction estimates.

research.abstract: Single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) and single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) bacteriophages form a key component of the global virome, yet the host genetic networks supporting their infection cycles remain poorly understood. Here we present a genome-wide map of the host factors involved in infection by F pilus-dependent ssRNA and ssDNA phages in Escherichia coli. Screens across ssRNA phages spanning all four genogroups of the Leviviricetes reveal a conserved network of host dependencies, with the notable exception of the F plasmid gene traD. Primary structural receptor components and DsbA-mediated disulfide bond formation are universally required to ensure F pilus integrity, whereas traD shows a strict genogroup-specific requirement during entry despite all lineages sharing the same receptor. Gene dosage screens identify elevated copy number of the genomic fragments encoding the HslU protease or the RNA chaperone StpA as barriers that restrict infection. Parallel assays with filamentous ssDNA phages confirm reliance on the host TolQRA complex for entry downstream of pilus engagement and track negative fitness signatures across envelope homeostasis clusters, reflecting the physiological burden of non-lytic virion extrusion. Comparative genomics and high-throughput genetics trace the selectivity of the isolation host, E. coli HSF, to a horizontally acquired Klebsiella capsule that excludes a large panel of double-stranded DNA phages isolated on other E. coli strains while allowing ssRNA and ssDNA virions to engage the extended F pilus and bypass the barrier through native pilus retraction. The work delivers a systematic, class-wide map of single-stranded phage-host interactions, a host platform for accessing uncultured viral diversity, and a functional blueprint for diagnostics, protein antibiotics and biocontrol tools that halt horizontal gene transfer.

research.abstract: Abstract Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) frequently coexists with infections, metabolic disease, cardiovascular disease, inflammatory lung injury and lung cancer. Molecular markers derived by comparing a comorbidity with healthy controls need not identify the transition from an established COPD state to that comorbidity. We therefore developed a two-stage computational strategy that asks a narrower question: which proteins can distinguish COPD samples from samples annotated with a specific COPD-associated comorbidity? First, a Human Protein Network (HPN; 17,302 proteins and 492,195 relationships) was encoded by 20 graph-derived features. A convolutional-neural-network ensemble, termed the functional-distance model (FDM), was trained on known drug-target–indication relationships. Stored training-set predictions yielded an apparent balanced accuracy of 0.811 and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.627; these values describe resubstitution performance and are not an independent estimate of generalization. The COPD-centred network search evaluated 2,645 nearby proteins and retained 224 candidates using a COPD FDM score above 0.50. Candidate expression was then tested in independently assembled public patient-derived transcriptomic data using simple one-feature classifiers and cross-validation. The resulting exploratory panel contained GTF2I for bacterial infection, UBXN7 for type 2 diabetes, LIFR for hypertension, SRGN for lung neoplasm and FGF4 for pneumonitis. Across the saved cross-validation predictions, balanced accuracy ranged from 0.838 to 0.970 and MCC from 0.726 to 0.941. SRGN has direct experimental support in non-small-cell lung cancer, whereas the remaining candidates have varying indirect mechanistic support and should be regarded as hypotheses rather than established disease biomarkers. This work demonstrates an orthogonal discovery framework in which network-based functional prioritization and patient-derived molecular discrimination constrain one another. Its main contribution is methodological: it provides a reusable strategy for generating comorbidity-specific biomarker hypotheses from an index-disease state. Prospective longitudinal cohorts are required before claims of progression prediction or clinical utility can be made.

Executed end-to-end via autonomous Native Rust bio-suite-supervisor optimization across 32 candidate RuNIE chains (total runtime 503.59 s; B = 1,000 UFBoot; 25,000 MCMC generations with 20% burn-in), RY3 purine/pyrimidine recoding under GTR+F+R4 reduces Sternorrhynchan compositional heterogeneity by 88.0% (RCFV = 0.0063 vs. 0.0525, ln L = -631,907.97), dating the Sternorrhyncha root to 234.6 Ma, Crown Aleyrodidae to 129.4 Ma, the Crown Bemisia tabaci cryptic species complex to 20.6 Ma, and the MED-MEAM1-IO crown divergence to 2.86 Ma. Native Rust quartet multispecies coalescent inference (runie-quartet-coalescent across 18 gene trees and 11,436,768 quartets in 89.77 ms) recovers 8,310,800 satisfied quartets (normalized Q = 0.7267, mean LPP = 0.8602) while ABBA-BABA tests quantify asymmetric MED-MEAM1 and SSA1-IO admixture. Sixty-one-state Goldman-Yang codon models identify strong purifying constraint on Orco chemosensation (omega_0 = 0.208) and Portiera bacteriocyte symbiosis alongside diversifying selection on salivary BtFer1/ALP hydrolases (omega_2 = 1.00) and CYP6CM1 substrate-recognition pockets (omega_2 = 1.00). Finally, 12 coupled Bayesian coalescent skylines contrast Old World savanna and agrarian expansions against New World founder bottlenecks and reveal sharp locus-specific effective population compressions at nuclear CYP6CM1 and ChE coding loci relative to neutral mitochondrial COX1 (1Ne) and Katoh E-INS-i-aligned nuclear ITS1-5.8S (4Ne) reservoirs. Autonomous 100% Native Rust bio-suite-supervisor synthesis across 544 verified NCBI records (L = 90,311 aligned columns, 32 RuNIE chains, 11.44M quartets, 300k MCMC generations in 503.59 s) resolves the 234.6 Ma-to-present Aleyrodidae and Bemisia radiation, CYP6CM1 selection, and 12 regional vs. multi-locus skylines. research.abstract: Summary Background Several randomised controlled trials of vitamin D supplementation for prevention of tuberculosis infection and disease have been conducted, but no individual participant data (IPD) meta-analysis has been conducted. Methods We conducted a systematic review, one-stage and two-stage IPD meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD420251173446) of double-blind, placebo-controlled randomised trials of vitamin D supplementation for prevention of tuberculosis infection or disease. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to October 29, 2026. The co-primary outcomes were incident tuberculosis infection (evidenced by tuberculin skin test or Interferon Gamma Release Assay conversion) and incident tuberculosis disease. Mixed-effects models estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs), accounting for trial and prespecified covariates. Prespecified subgroup analyses investigated effect modification by sex and age, body-mass index, vitamin D status, and BCG vaccination status. Findings Four trials contributed IPD for 14,619 participants. Vitamin D did not reduce risk of incident tuberculosis infection (9,557 participants; aOR 0.97, 95% CI 0.81-1.18; p=0.79) or incident tuberculosis disease (14,533 participants; aOR 0.78, 95% CI 0.56-1.10; p=0.15). There was no evidence of effect modification by participant characteristics investigated in sub-group analyses, including in participants with 25-hydroxyvitamin D <25 nmol/L (infection: aOR 0.95, 95% CI 0.67-1.34; disease: 1.01, 0.45-2.30). Serious adverse events and mortality were unaffected. Interpretation Vitamin D supplementation did not reduce the risk of incident tuberculosis infection or disease in the populations studied, either overall or within sub-groups. The 95% confidence interval of the effect estimate for prevention of tuberculosis disease remains compatible with a potentially important benefit, and further trials for this indication may be warranted.

research.abstract: DEG (Degradation of periplasmic proteins) proteases are ATP-independent serine endopeptidases found in bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotes including plants. They are considered to be key regulators of development and stress tolerance in plants. In this study, a comprehensive genome-wide analysis identified 19 serine protease-like DEG family proteins in potato (Solanum tuberosum L.), revealing their structural diversity, domain architecture, and regulatory potential. Physiochemical profiling showed a predominance of acidic isoelectric points (pI), variable protein lengths (169–1083 amino acids), and differential stability indices. Subcellular localization predicted most DEG proteases to reside in the chloroplast, with others distributed across cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondria, and peroxisome. Domain analysis confirmed the universal presence of the trypsin domain, with varying numbers of PDZ domains and additional conserved motifs among paralogs. Evolutionary divergence analysis of StDEG genes and their orthologs from six Solanaceae species as well as Arabidopsis thaliana, Oryza sativa, and Zea mays revealed dN/dS ratios below one for all orthologous pairs, suggesting that StDEG genes have evolved under strong purifying selection and remained highly conserved throughout plant evolution. Gene ontology annotations linked DEG proteases to key biological functions including PSII repair, photoinhibition, and chloroplast organization, alongside protein catabolism and light stimulus response. Promoter analysis revealed an abundance of cis-regulatory elements (CREs), particularly light-responsive motifs, along with hormone and stress-related elements such as ABRE, ARE, and MBS. Expression profiling across eight developmental tissues demonstrated tissue-specific expression patterns, with strong transcript accumulation of selected DEG members in senescent leaf, stolon, shoot apex, and tuber. Interestingly, several splice variants showed unique expression dynamics, including stage-specific and stress-induced activation. Upon exposure to abiotic and hormonal cues, 16 DEG proteases displayed significant transcriptional modulation, particularly under light, ABA, and Zeatin treatments, with notable fold changes reaching up to 26-fold in certain variants. These findings highlight the functional versatility of DEG proteases in potato development and stress adaptation, especially their responsiveness to light and hormonal stimuli. The characterization of these proteases paves the way for future studies on their roles in crop resilience and genome editing applications.

research.abstract: The family Noctuidae includes agricultural pests that vary in geographic distribution and host range. This study analyzed 30 mitogenomes representing 14 noctuid species; Ostrinia nubilalis (Crambidae) served as the phylogenetic outgroup. The genomes contained the typical complement of 37 mitochondrial genes and exhibited conserved gene order, pronounced A + T enrichment, and a preference for A/T-ending synonymous codons. A neutrality regression based on species means revealed a modest positive association between GC3 and GC12 (R 2 = 0.3201; p = 0.03494), although it could not distinguish the respective contributions of mutation and selection. Maximum-likelihood and Bayesian analyses of 13 protein-coding genes (11,229 bp) agreed on 26 of the 28 internal groupings in the maximum-likelihood tree, including a strongly supported Spodoptera clade. Differences in deeper relationships occurred at nodes with limited support. All 13 genes had dN/dS estimates below one (0.00306-0.01691), consistent with purifying selection. Codon usage varied among gene categories, and gene-wise codon bias was not significantly associated with dN/dS. Five crop-associated species with multiple larval host plants and documented long-distance migration- Helicoverpa armigera, Athetis lepigone, Spodoptera litura, S. frugiperda, and Mamestra brassicae -fell below the fitted neutrality regression line. Whether their ecological traits relate to this pattern remains requires broader taxonomic sampling and ecological data in future investigations.

research.abstract: A bstract Understanding the mechanisms facilitating the repeated evolution of traits is a core question in evolutionary biology. While repeated evolution has been observed across many systems, behavioral phenotypes have been less well studied than morphological traits. Migration is a behavioral adaptation to seasonality that has evolved independently in many animals, and repeated gains and losses of migratory behavior have been especially prevalent throughout the diversification of birds. While migratory traits are heritable in many taxa and candidate genes underlying intraspecific variation in migratory behavior have been identified, whether similar genetic changes are responsible for the repeated evolution of migration remains poorly understood. We used a phylogenomic approach to investigate the relationship between variation in candidate genes and migratory propensity across nearly all species in the parulid warbler radiation ( n = 101), a group of songbirds in which migratory behavior has been lost and gained multiple times. Comparisons of candidate gene tree topologies to the parulid warbler species tree revealed cases of discordance, though these were explained by differences in the number of phylogenetically informative sites among genes rather than by elevated genetic similarity among species sharing migratory strategies. Testing models of coding sequence evolution identified sites with elevated dN/dS in five candidate genes, suggestive of positive selection; however, variation at these sites showed no clear association with migratory strategy, nor did we detect recurrent selection across lineages where transitions in migratory behavior most likely occurred. Together, these results contradict the hypothesis that selection on shared variation (ancestral polymorphisms or introgressed alleles) facilitated the repeated evolution of migration in this clade.

research.abstract: Abstract Genome-wide association and other genetic studies have identified genes involved in disease pathogenesis, and their encoded proteins have provided therapeutic targets. However, little is known about which cells are the functional home of these disease-associated genes and proteins. Single-cell technologies are enabling high-resolution profiling of cell phenotypes and revealing cellular contexts of disease, yet much of the resulting knowledge remains embedded in individual datasets and scientific literature. To address these gaps, the National Library of Medicine has developed Cell Knowledge Network (NLM-CKN, https://nlm-ckn.org ). Reproducible computational workflows have generated cell phenotype knowledge for 2,585 cell sets and 5,139 selectively expressed genes from 88 datasets covering 10 human organs. Mapping of these cell sets to cell types grounds Cell Ontology terms in experimental evidence. This experimental knowledge is integrated with external knowledge of anatomical and cell-type hierarchies, gene-disease associations, and therapeutic interventions. A semantic schema defines node types and relations, enabling knowledge to be transformed into triple assertions and loaded into an ArangoDB database with provenance and quantitative evidence. The NLM-CKN interface supports graphical exploration of the cellular constituents of healthy human tissues. Finally, topological analyses generate insights into cellular contributions to disease pathogenesis, cellular contexts for therapeutic intervention, and drug-repurposing hypotheses.

research.abstract: Abstract Caspase-1 and -11 are inflammatory caspases that trigger pyroptosis, yet in most infection models they confer only a modest survival benefit. We have proposed that caspase-1 and -11 evolved primarily to defend against ubiquitous environmental microbes that have not been under selective pressure to evade them, whereas host-adapted pathogens have evolved evasion strategies. Testing this idea is complicated because the inbred mouse strains used in most infection studies carry mutations in innate immune genes: i.e., C57BL/6 (B6) mice carry a loss-of-function Nramp1 allele, and 129 mice lack functional caspase-11. Here we generated B6 × 129 F1 hybrid mice, which are gene-sufficient at both Nramp1 and Casp11 , and used them to measure the fold change in lethal dose (ΔLD 100 ) caused by caspase-1 and -11 deficiency for four pathogens on the B6, 129, and F1 backgrounds. Caspase-1 and -11 conferred little or no survival benefit against the host-adapted pathogens Listeria monocytogenes and Salmonella Typhimurium on any of the three backgrounds, apart from a modest benefit at the lowest S . Typhimurium inoculum in F1 mice. In contrast, caspase-1 and -11 were required to survive infection with the environmental pathogens Burkholderia thailandensis and Chromobacterium violaceum , where caspase-1 and -11 deficiency lowered the lethal dose by up to six orders of magnitude. The failure of caspase-1 and -11 against host-adapted pathogens therefore persists on a genetically robust hybrid background, supporting the view that a major evolutionary role of caspase-1 and -11 is defense against environmental microbes that have not been selected to evade them. Importance Cells can sense bacteria growing inside them and destroy themselves, killing the invader along with the cell. Two enzymes, caspase-1 and caspase-11, carry this out, yet mice lacking both die from host-adapted bacteria such as Salmonella and Listeria almost as readily as normal mice. We proposed that these enzymes instead evolved to stop the ubiquitous bacteria of soil and water, microbes that have never faced selective pressure to hide from them. Testing this has been difficult because the standard inbred strains each carry defective immune genes. We crossed two strains to produce hybrid mice with a complete set, then measured the dose of bacteria needed to kill them. Caspase-1 and caspase-11 gave almost no protection against Salmonella or Listeria , but raised the lethal dose of the environmental bacteria Burkholderia thailandensis and Chromobacterium violaceum by up to a millionfold. This defense therefore appears aimed at environmental microbes.

research.abstract: Zoonotic tuberculosis (zTB), caused by animal-adapted members of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC), is classically attributed to M. bovis but is increasingly linked to M. orygis across South Asia. Species-level MTBC identification is rarely performed in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), leaving the zTB burden poorly defined. Bangladesh has endemic bovine tuberculosis, a growing dairy sector, unpasteurised-milk consumption, and expanding captive wildlife collections, yet the evidence has not been synthesised by diagnostic reliability. This systematic evidence map aimed to collate the evidence on zTB in Bangladesh and to review the diagnostic methods used to identify animal-adapted MTBC species, particularly M. bovis and M. orygis , in livestock, wildlife, and humans. Following PRISMA 2020, we searched PubMed, Google Scholar, and BanglaJOL from the 1970s to June 2026; CAB Abstracts, Scopus, and Web of Science were not accessible. Two reviewers independently screened and appraised studies using the JBI checklist, assigning each to a five-level diagnostic evidence hierarchy (Level 1: WGS, phylogeny, RD typing, spoligotyping, or MLVA; Level 5: tuberculin skin test or serology only). These non-comparable tests precluded meta-analysis; therefore, findings are presented as an evidence map. Thirty-five studies met the inclusion criteria: 24 on prevalence in cattle/buffaloes, 10 on molecular diagnosis and characterisation in cattle, captive wildlife, and humans, and 1 specifically on molecular diagnosis and characterisation in humans. Most livestock studies used non-discriminatory tests (tuberculin skin tests, ELISA, or untyped PCR) and reported non-comparable reactor proportions of 1.2% to 33.7%. The few studies using species-level methods (Levels 1–2) confirmed M. orygis in cattle and in at least seven captive wildlife species, including monkeys, using marker-based molecular assays. Several historical reports of M. bovis were based on non-discriminatory PCR or serology, which cannot reliably distinguish among MTBC members. Human evidence was limited to three studies, including one WGS-confirmed M. orygis case identified through tuberculosis surveillance. In published reports from Bangladesh, M. orygis is the only animal-adapted MTBC member molecularly confirmed at the cattle–wildlife–human interface; existing M. bovis claims lack discriminatory support and require cautious reinterpretation. zTB surveillance should therefore move beyond an M. bovis -only framework and integrate species-level MTBC identification into a staged, resource-appropriate One Health strategy across animal, wildlife, and human health.

items.title: Salinity adaptation in date palm (Phoenix dactylifera): evidence for selective sweeps at Salt Overly Sensitive (SOS) genes

research.abstract: ABSTRACT The date palm is a high salinity tolerant fruit tree grown mainly in the region spanning from North Africa to parts of South Asia. Climate change models of this region indicate the possibility of increasing salinity in the future. The Salt Overly Sensitive (SOS) pathway is crucial for salinity tolerance in plants, serving as a primary defense mechanism by facilitating sodium exclusion. To better understand date palms’ salt tolerance, we analyzed variation in SOS pathway genes in a set of 197 date palm genomes collected from across the range of cultivation. Here, we show evidence for selective sweeps in multiple SOS pathway genes. A single major pdSOS1 haplotype is at very high frequency in Eastern and Western subpopulations, with a minor, likely ancestral haplotype still present in both geographical locations. Allele-specific gene expression analysis showed differences in salt-treated roots between swept and ancestral haplotypes. Interestingly, sequence-based analysis of the pdSOS1 haplotype suggested a second, much earlier introgression event between P. theophrasti and date palm, though direction is unclear. This event happened before both the selective sweep and the previously reported recent introgression to date palm. We identified a MITE transposable element inserted into a pdSOS1 intron on the swept haplotype, and a similar insertion was found in an intron of the SOS2 paralog pdCIPK8 . Both insertions are unique to date palm among Phoenix species. The pdCIPK8 haplotype containing the MITE is also at high frequency in both populations. Further analysis showed evidence for a selective sweep spanning the pdSOS3 region in the western population that shares similarity to an Eastern haplotype spanning the promoter region only. Slower extended haplotype homozygosity decay surrounding the genes in the western population suggests that the swept haplotype originated in the East and spread to the West in all cases. Altogether, our data provide evidence of selective sweeps in the date palm SOS pathway and may go to explaining how this species has developed such high salinity tolerance.

research.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Sputum culture conversion in patients with pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) is the most important interim indicator for drug-resistant (DR) tuberculosis (TB) treatment effectiveness. Bedaquiline-based regimens offer the possibility of more effective and less toxic treatment for DR TB. Bedaquiline-based regimens have been adopted as the new standard of care for DR TB, replacing the oto-and nephrotoxic aminoglycosides. We determined the median time to sputum culture conversion (TTCC) and associated factors among RR and MDR TB patients treated with Bedaquiline-based regimens, at Mulago National Referral Hospital, Uganda. METHODS: In a longitudinal type of observational study performed at Mulago Hospital, between January 2020 and June 2023, RR and MDR TB patients' records were reviewed to obtain data on socio-demographic and clinical factors, and TTCC. The study outcome was TTCC, recorded as time from RR/MDR TB treatment initiation to sputum culture conversion, which was defined as at least 2 consecutive negative TB sputum cultures, at least 30 days apart, for a RR/MDR PTB patient who was sputum culture positive at baseline. Analysis for median TTCC was done using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and the log-logistic parametric survival regression model was used to identify predictors for TTCC. RESULTS: Of the 265 participants, 196 (74.0%) were male, with median age of 35(IQR:27-42) years. The median TTCC was 7 (IQR:4-8) weeks from treatment initiation. Grade 2 + baseline smear positivity (adjusted Time Ratio (aTR):1.24, 95% CI:1.02-1.51, p = 0.029), grade 3 + baseline smear positivity (aTR:1.62, 95% CI:1.30-2.01, p < 0.001), cavitary disease on CXR (aTR:1.36, 95% CI:1.18-1.56, p < 0.001), and pleural effusion on CXR (aTR:1.81, 95% CI:1.43-2.31, p < 0.001) significantly prolonged the TTCC. Diabetes mellitus (7/265) significantly reduced the TTCC (aTR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.22 - 0.60, p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: The WHO long regimen (9 months) was indistinguishable from the shorter 6-months regimen for the time to culture conversion. Integration of TB screening at points of care of high-risk patients like diabetics remains important for early detection and prompt initiation of DR TB treatment for better outcomes. The TB program and clinicians should enhance and individualize support for RR/MDR TB patients with more severe disease, to ensure optimum TTCC and successful treatment outcomes. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

research.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis remains the leading cause of death from a single infectious pathogen globally despite decades of effective chemotherapy. In 2024, an estimated 10·7 million people developed tuberculosis, including approximately 620 000 people living with HIV (PLHIV), and tuberculosis caused an estimated 1·23 million deaths overall, including approximately 150 000 deaths among PLHIV. Men accounted for more than half of the cases, and children represented a substantial burden, reflecting ongoing transmission and diagnostic gaps. Approximately a quarter of the world's population has been infected with M tuberculosis, with immunological evidence of previous or current infection. This population includes groups at increased risk of progression to tuberculosis disease, particularly those with recent infection, HIV, undernutrition, young age, or other clinical and social vulnerabilities. Following 3 years of COVID-19-related setbacks, global tuberculosis incidence declined modestly (1%) from 2023 to 2024 but remains higher than in 2020 and far off-track to meet the 2025 WHO End TB Strategy milestones. Case detection improved to 8·3 million notifications (78% of estimated incident cases), supported by expanded molecular diagnostics; however, prevalence surveys continue to reveal substantial proportions of bacteriologically confirmed but asymptomatic tuberculosis, highlighting persistent transmission and missed diagnoses. 30 high-burden countries accounted for 87% of cases, led by India, Indonesia, the Philippines, China, Pakistan, Nigeria, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Bangladesh. M tuberculosis-HIV co-infection remains a major driver of mortality in sub-Saharan Africa. Drug-resistant tuberculosis threatens progress: of 390 000 estimated multidrug-resistant or rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis cases in 2024, only 42% initiated treatment, although treatment success improved to 71%. Tuberculosis-preventive treatment reached 5·3 million people, including 58% of PLHIV and 25% of eligible household contacts, well below global targets. Persistent undernutrition, poverty, HIV, diabetes, smoking, alcohol use, air pollution, migration, and conflict continue to shape tuberculosis epidemiology. With financing at only 27% of global targets, accelerated prevention, proactive case finding, social protection, and sustained political commitment are essential to eliminate tuberculosis.

research.abstract: Abstract The Wnt gene family plays a central role in vertebrate development, yet its evolutionary dynamics across lineages remain largely unexplored. Here, we present the most comprehensive analysis of Wnt gene evolution in vertebrates to date, leveraging a large-scale comparative genomics approach of 38,886 Wnt gene sequences mined from 1,961 species. We first investigate overall patterns of gene retention, duplication, and loss, and then focus specifically on the impact of whole-genome duplications (WGDs). We uncover striking variation in Wnt gene repertoire sizes, with ray-finned fishes (Actinopterygii) exhibiting the largest repertoires – even after excluding taxa with recent WGDs. Notably, we identify extreme expansions in polyploid cyprinids, including an octoploid hybrid harbouring 99 Wnt genes, the highest number observed. Unexpectedly elevated Wnt copy numbers in diploid species, such as in the Antarctic lanternfish (Electrona antarctica) and the brook lamprey (Lethenteron reissneri), point to lineage-specific expansions, although the potential adaptive significance of these expansions remains to be tested. Evolutionary rate analyses reveal that certain Wnt clades – especially Wnt8 and Wnt16 – exhibit elevated dN/dS ratios and high birth–death rates, consistent with repeated episodes of relaxed constraint and/or adaptive diversification. Contrary to our expectations, there was no relationship between developmental expression timing and evolutionary rates, suggesting pleiotropic regulation and functional redundancy of Wnt genes. Altogether, our findings reveal widespread variation in Wnt copy number and turnover among lineages, shaped by both genome duplication history and divergent evolutionary trajectories. This work provides a high-resolution framework for understanding the molecular evolution of a key developmental toolkit and highlights candidate genes for future studies of vertebrate eco-morphological diversity.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Listeria monocytogenes is a Gram-positive bacterial foodborne pathogen responsible for the severe illness listeriosis. Of the 14 L. monocytogenes serotypes, serotype 4b is a major contributor to human listeriosis and encompasses all four leading hypervirulent clonal complexes (CCs), including the ancient, ubiquitous CC2. CC2 is globally dominated by sublineage (SL) 2, responsible for most human CC2-associated cases. Here we describe two other CC2 SLs, SLs 782 and 1039. These SLs are newly recognized, having been reported only since 2002, and to date are encountered exclusively in North America. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that they are strikingly divergent from each other as well as from SL2. SL782 and SL1039 have been implicated in human listeriosis and have also been repeatedly isolated from surface water and wildlife in North America, with several of these environmental strains exhibiting high genomic similarity (≤7 core genome allelic mismatches) to strains from human listeriosis. They share an unusual resistance profile towards a panel of Listeria wide-host-range-phages and exhibit several distinct lineage-specific traits. Specifically, SL782 universally lacks a gene otherwise unique to and conserved in serotype 4b and harbors the Listeria pathogenicity island LIPI-4, while SL1039 harbors LIPI-3 and is almost always resistant to tetracycline, harboring the novel Tn 916 -like transposon Tn 916 . 1039 . These and other traits may have driven clonal emergence of SL782 and SL1039, potentially via adaptations in natural ecosystems. IMPORTANCE Listeria monocytogenes causes the severe foodborne illness listeriosis and the hypervirulent clonal complex (CC) 2 is a major contributor to human disease. Most CC2 strains belong to the long-recognized, ubiquitous sublineage (SL) 2. Surprisingly, the two other leading SLs within CC2, SL782 and 1039, have been isolated exclusively from North America, and only subsequently to 2002. They differ remarkably from each other and other CC2 strains and exhibit unusual genomic and phenotypic traits. They have been repeatedly isolated from watersheds and wildlife, with such environmental isolates exhibiting high genomic similarity to those from human listeriosis. The findings are important in identifying novel, unexpected features in the composition and evolution of a major, hypervirulent L. monocytogenes CC. They will also serve as platforms for further studies to further elucidate the reservoirs, emergence, persistence, and dissemination of novel Listeria sublineages and their roles in the continuum between natural ecosystems and human disease.

research.abstract: Introduction Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a critical threat to global health security and disproportionately affects children in sub-Saharan Africa. In Nigeria, the burden of multidrug-resistant pathogens in paediatric populations is increasing; however, data from the South-South region, particularly Edo State, remain scarce. This study aims to determine the prevalence, patterns and transmission dynamics of AMR among paediatric patients in Edo State, Nigeria, using a One Health approach that integrates human, animal and environmental health interfaces. Methods and analysis This mixed-methods study will enrol 455 hospitalised children (<18 years) at the University of Benin Teaching Hospital (UBTH). Clinical (urine, blood, rectal and nasopharyngeal swabs), environmental and animal samples will be collected to isolate and characterise locally recoverable bacterial pathogens prioritised with reference to the WHO 2024 priority pathogen list. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing will be performed using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method in accordance with Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute guidelines. Selected clinically or epidemiologically important resistant isolates will be stored at -80°C for possible future molecular characterisation, resources permitting. Key informant interviews with caregivers, healthcare providers and policymakers will explore the systemic enablers and barriers to paediatric AMR stewardship. Quantitative data will be analysed using descriptive statistics and logistic regression, while qualitative data will undergo thematic analysis guided by Braun and Clarke's framework. Ethics and dissemination Ethical approval has been obtained from the UBTH Health Research Ethics Committee (Ref: ADM/E 22/A/VOL.VII/14831247). Written informed consent will be obtained from all participants. Findings will inform antibiotic stewardship, strengthen surveillance and guide AMR policy at institutional, state and national levels. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, policy briefs, institutional reports and engagement with national and international health agencies.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with various adverse outcomes, but links with subsequent violent victimisation are uncertain. Methods We linked data from Swedish sociodemographic and medical registers to create a matched cohort of people with diagnosed PTSD and a comparison sample matched on birth year, sex, and county of residence in the year preceding diagnosis (or matching in the case of undiagnosed individuals). We calculated the cumulative incidence of violent victimisation (defined using ICD codes registered at hospitalisation) and conducted stratified Cox regression analyses, adjusted for parental factors, psychiatric comorbidities, and history of violent victimisation. Findings The cohort contained 29,688 individuals diagnosed with PTSD, who were matched with 296,880 individuals without PTSD (78.6% female), and followed for up to 34 years. Individuals with PTSD had higher cumulative incidences of violent victimisation after their index diagnosis (18.7% compared to 2.7% at 25 years follow-up). Individuals with both a diagnosis of PTSD and history of violent victimisation had the highest cumulative incidence (28.7%). After adjustment for parental characteristics, prior psychiatric comorbidity and prior violent victimisation, PTSD was associated with an adjusted hazard ratio of 4.0 (95% CI 3.7–4.4). Interpretation Preventing subsequent violent victimisation among individuals diagnosed with PTSD should be considered by clinical services and incorporated into violence prevention strategies. Funding AP is funded by the Wellcome Trust (grant code 218497/Z/19/Z). SF and AS are supported by the NIHR Oxford Health Biomedical Research Centre (grant BRC-1215-20005). No funder(s) listed had any role in the design or implementation of this study.

research.abstract: INTRODUCTION: TB (tuberculosis) due to Mycobacterium tuberculosis continues to be a significant worldwide health issue. Timely and reliable diagnostic tests will improve treatment outcomes and reduce the spread of disease. Traditional TB diagnostics currently available, such as smear microscopy and culture, have significant limitations with regard to sensitivity and turnaround times, especially for smear-negative cases and for tuberculosis in extrapulmonary locations. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this review is to analyze the evolution of TB diagnostics from traditional microbiology to new molecular diagnostic methods (including CRISPR, biosensor technology, and microfluidic methods), including an assessment of their diagnostic testing performance, feasibility, and potential for the future. METHODS: The systematic narrative review aimed to systematically assess literature published from 2020 to 2025 retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar. The review was carried out according to the PRISMA guidelines and included 89 studies after screening and assessing for eligibility. The data were analysed qualitatively (i.e., through thematic analysis) by comparing data from conventional, molecular, and next-generation diagnostic methods. RESULTS: Molecular tests (e.g., GeneXpert, Line Probe Assays, PCR, and Whole Genome Sequencing) provide greater sensitivity and specificity than traditional methods and allow for faster diagnosis. Additionally, newer CRISPR-based tests, biosensors, and microfluidic devices hold promise for rapid, portable, point-of-care diagnosis of tuberculosis. DISCUSSION: The findings indicate that molecular diagnostics improve rapid detection and drug-resistance profiling, while CRISPR and biosensor platforms offer potential for rapid point-of-care testing. However, affordability, infrastructure, clinical validation, and scalability remain important barriers. CONCLUSION: The use of molecular diagnostic testing, CRISPR technology, biosensors, artificial intelligence, and portable platforms will dramatically enhance existing TB surveillance systems and strategies for controlling the disease globally.

research.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis , remains a major global health challenge, further exacerbated by the rapid emergence of drug-resistant strains. Despite continuous efforts, the discovery of novel anti-TB agents has lagged behind the evolution of resistance, largely due to the limitations of conventional experimental pipelines and the growing biological complexity of the pathogen. In recent years, computational drug discovery approaches—including virtual screening, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven modeling, and hybrid computational frameworks—have substantially expanded the chemical space accessible for early-stage anti-TB research. However, their translational success remains limited. This discrepancy reflects a fundamental mismatch between target-centric computational paradigms and the multi-scale biological constraints of Mtb , including permeability barriers, efflux mechanisms, metabolic state heterogeneity, lesion-level pharmacokinetics, and regimen-dependent therapeutic effects. This review critically evaluates current computational strategies for anti-TB drug screening, with particular emphasis on their performance under TB-specific biological and resistance constraints. We further explore computational approaches designed to address drug-resistant Mtb , including resistance-aware compound design, host-directed therapy, and combination regimen modeling. Finally, we explore key limitations in current computational pipelines, including challenges in data quality, biological integration, and regimen-level modeling, and propose a shift toward biologically grounded, regimen-aware, and systems-level frameworks. Bridging the gap between in silico prediction and clinical efficacy will require integrating multi-scale biological realism into computational pipelines, enabling more reliable translation of computational advances into effective anti-TB therapeutics.

research.abstract: Background Toll-like receptor genes have been extensively researched for their role in the susceptibility to pulmonary tuberculosis across different populations. The relationship between variations in toll-like receptor genes and additional risk factors for pulmonary tuberculosis is not well understood, because of the complex interplay between genetic predispositions and environmental influences. This study aimed to elucidate the association of TLR2 T597C, TLR4 A896G, and TLR9 G1174A gene polymorphisms with the risk of developing pulmonary tuberculosis. Methods A total of 306 samples – 153 patients with pulmonary tuberculosis and 153 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were selected using a consecutive sampling technique. Clinical and biochemical variables were measured to assess the associated risk factors. Deoxyribonucleic acid was isolated from blood samples, and the TLR2 , TLR4, and TLR9 genotypes were identified using polymerase chain reaction–restriction fragment length polymorphism and analyzed by agarose gel electrophoresis. Results Our analysis showed that the TLR2 -CC genotype (OR = 3.82; 95% CI = 1.79–8.16; P < 0.001) and C allele (OR=2.12; 95%CI: 1.42–3.10; P < 0.001), the TLR4 -GG genotype (OR=3.18; 95%CI: 1.71–5.92; P < 0.001) and G allele (OR=2.25; 95%CI: 1.61–3.14; P < 0.001), and the TLR9 -AA genotype (OR=2.00; 95%CI: 1.09–3.68; P = 0.025) and A allele (OR=1.60; 95%CI: 1.15–2.21; P < 0.001) is significantly associated in patients than in controls, suggesting their potential role as genetic risk factors for the development of pulmonary tuberculosis. Combined genotype analysis revealed that individuals carrying all three risk genotypes (CC-GG-AA) significantly associated with increased PTB risk. Multivariable analysis showed that HIV co-infection and malnutrition were independent predictors of pulmonary tuberculosis. Conclusion The TLR2 T597C gene of the CC genotype and the C allele, the TLR4 A896G genes of the GG genotype and the G allele, and the TLR9 G1174A genes of the AA genotype and the A allele are associated with increased risk of pulmonary tuberculosis among the Ethiopian patients under study.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Species in the Rosaceae tribe Spiraeeae occupy diverse habitats and vary strikingly in growth form and leaf morphology. Still, no reference transcriptomes have been published for the tribe, and its transcriptome‐level variation is uncharacterized. We generated long‐read (PacBio Iso‐Seq) reference transcriptomes of five species spanning three genera: Petrophytum caespitosum (Nutt.) Rydb., Spiraea lucida Douglas ex Greene, Spiraea splendens Baumann ex K. Koch, Aruncus dioicus (Walter) Fernald var. dioicus , and Aruncus aethusifolius (H.Lév.) Nakai. We then quantified expression across 20 individuals using 3′‐tag RNA sequencing (TagSeq) to characterize expression patterns, ortholog sequence divergence, and gene repertoire. Multivariate analyses (principal component analysis [PCA] and hierarchical clustering) resolved replicates into three groups corresponding to the sampled genera. Because the material combined field‐collected and potted plants, we treat expression comparisons as descriptive and do not attribute them to genetic control of interspecific differences. Pairwise analyses revealed extensive transcriptional divergence between genera, including thousands of differentially expressed transcripts in comparisons such as A. aethusifolius vs. P. caespitosum . Functional enrichment highlighted variation in transport and catabolism, plastid organization, and biotic‐stress responses, implicating both metabolic and organelle‐associated processes. Transcription factor families, particularly bHLH and bZIP, varied most among differentially expressed transcripts. Weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA) recovered modules correlated with species identity; because between‐species variation dominates this dataset, we treat these as descriptive summaries of coexpression structure and do not regard them as independent evidence of species‐specific regulatory programs. Because reads were quantified against a reference assembled from species‐specific contigs, mapping rates were higher within species (70.5%–85.1%) than across species (25.1%–77.0%), and between‐species expression comparisons are interpreted with this asymmetry in mind. Sequence‐level analysis of orthologous transcript pairs indicated that protein‐coding genes are predominantly under purifying selection. A small fraction (2.7%–5.0% of retained pairs) showed Ka/Ks > 1, but these were concentrated at low synonymous divergence, where ratio estimates are unstable; we therefore treat them as screening‐level candidates for rapid divergence, enriched for stress‐response, membrane‐trafficking, and ion‐transport annotations, and we make no claim of positive selection. These results provide a comparative transcriptomic framework for Spiraeeae and identify candidate transcripts and protein‐coding differences for future studies of ecological and morphological variation in Rosaceae.

research.abstract: Computing phylogenetic likelihoods becomes challenging when the continuous-time Markov chain has a large state space. At each branch, pruning algorithms require terms of the form $e^{Q t}\cdot B$, where $Q$ is an $S \times S$ rate matrix (e.g., for $S$ states), $t$ is a branch length, and the columns of matrix $B$ (e.g., $B \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{S \times L}$) are partial-likelihood vectors for $L$ site patterns. Many implementations calculate the dense transition matrix $P(t)=e^{Q t}$ via eigendecomposition and multiply it by $B$. This strategy is efficient for small state spaces, but it can be inefficient for large sparse rate matrices because forming $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices destroys sparsity and its cost may not be well amortized when $L$ is small. We implement an alternative likelihood kernel based on the Al-Mohy and Higham (2011) algorithm for computing the action of the matrix exponential directly, avoiding explicit construction of $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices. The resulting method takes full advantage of the sparsity of $Q$. We implement this method as a CPU-based extension to the BEAGLE library and evaluate it on two large-state molecular models: a Markov-modulated codon model of heterotachy with $M$ selective regimes and $61\cdot M$ possible states, and a codon-pair model of interlocus gene conversion between two paralogs with $61^2=3\,721$ possible states. Our results characterize when action-based likelihood computation improves performance over calculating $e^{Q t}$ directly. We show that this method enables fast, scalable inference for complex models, removing a key computational barrier to the study of evolution with large state space models.
