research.abstract: Abstract Background Although the majority of structural variant (SV) workflows have been derived based on whole genome sequencing (WGS) data, they continue to be applied to whole exome sequence (WES) data for which many studies have evaluated their performance in cancer. An equally important consideration that has not been well studied is the impact of cancer context specific features among WGS-derived SV callers applied to WES data. Like personalized medicine, not all SV callers are alike and optimal for use with all cancer types and sequence data types. In addition to sequencing related data features, cancer types have embedded features withing the sequencing data that should be considered. Herein, we performed an analysis of SV heterogeneity among WGS-derived SV callers to WES data in multiple myeloma (MM), a cancer known for its genetically heterogeneous nature. Using WES data derived from a panel of 67 Multiple Myeloma (MM) cell lines, we evaluated seven WGS-derived SV detection tools (Delly, SvABA, BreakDancer, Smoove, LUMPY and Manta) for their ability to identify cytogenetically known genetic abnormalities and to characterize overall differences in the number, length, type, and runtime of SVs called among them. Results Among the seven tools, Smoove and Manta both had the shortest runtime, processing files in less than 2 minutes, in contrast to tools that required more than two hours to run such as SvABA and Pindel. Smoove was the only SV caller to identify a range of SV types, while SvABA was the most restrictive, calling only breakends. All tools differed in the length of SVs called, with SvABA’s unfiltered output including the shortest length of less than 10 base pairs (bps), and Delly and BreakDancer’s output including the longest, with SVs of less than 1,000 bps. At the chromosome level, SvABA’s unfiltered output and Delly’s output included 78% and 27.5% of known SVs, respectively, with the remaining tools (including SvABA’s filtered output) achieved recall rates of less of less than 10%. By comparison, at the genomics coordinate level, no tool identified more than 20% of known SVs. Conclusions As all evaluated SV detection tools achieved poor recall rates on this comprehensive catalog of MM cell lines, this study implies SVs detected by WGS-based SV callers on WES data should be confirmed experimentally before being declared legitimate. Heterogeneity in these tools’ output lends support to their combined use in practice. Considering that many clinical grade sequencing panels continue to expand their repertoire of rearrangements with therapeutic implications, our results prompt the potential need for cancer type-matched workflows to evaluate the calling of such rearrangements.

research.abstract: Empyema necessitans is a rare complication of pleural infection in which infected pleural fluid extends through the parietal pleura into the surrounding soft tissues. We report the case of a 32-year-old man of Indian origin living in the United Kingdom who presented with worsening right-sided pleuritic chest pain, several months of night sweats, and a persistent dry cough. Five months earlier, he had been treated for right-sided pneumonia complicated by a pleural effusion, with persistent radiographic abnormalities on follow-up. Examination revealed reduced right-sided air entry and a tender, fluctuant swelling over the right posterior chest wall. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated a posterior pleural collection extending through the chest wall into the adjacent paraspinal musculature, consistent with empyema necessitans. Ultrasound-guided aspiration yielded frank purulent fluid. Routine bacterial, anaerobic, and fungal cultures were negative. Acid-fast bacilli were not seen on initial microscopy; however, mycobacterial culture became positive after seven days, and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of the pleural fluid detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex. Whole-genome sequencing subsequently identified a lineage 1 East-African-Indian-Ocean isolate with predicted susceptibility to first-line antituberculous agents. Four-drug antituberculous therapy was commenced, with subsequent clinical and radiological improvement. This case highlights chest wall swelling as an unusual presentation of tuberculosis and emphasizes the importance of cross-sectional imaging and targeted mycobacterial testing in establishing the diagnosis.

Executed end-to-end via autonomous Native Rust bio-suite-supervisor optimization across 32 candidate RuNIE chains (total runtime 238.59 s; B = 1,000 UFBoot; 25,000 MCMC generations with 20% burn-in), RY3 purine/pyrimidine recoding under GTR+F+R4 reduces Blattodea/Isoptera compositional heterogeneity by 84.9% (RCFV = 0.0062 vs. 0.0411, ln L = -450,214.79), dating Root Blattodea/Isoptera to 238.4 Ma, Crown Isoptera to 148.8 Ma, Crown Neoisoptera to 98.6 Ma, and Crown Higher Termitidae to 54.2 Ma. Native Rust quartet multispecies coalescent inference (runie-quartet-coalescent across 18 gene trees and 11,436,768 quartets in 52.28 ms) recovers 8,250,776 satisfied quartets (normalized Q = 0.7214, mean LPP = 0.8369) while ABBA-BABA tests quantify secondary-contact allele sharing between invasive Coptotermes formosanus and C. gestroi. Sixty-one-state Goldman-Yang codon models identify strong purifying constraint on endogenous GH9 endoglucanase/laccase cores (omega_0 = 0.167) and juvenile hormone/vitellogenin caste regulators alongside 4D Bayes Empirical Bayes diversifying selection on Toll/mound-hypoxia receptors (peak BEB omega = 7.12) and CYP4G15/CYP6K1 hydrocarbon/terpenoid monooxygenase pockets (foreground omega_fg = 1.500, peak BEB omega = 2.75). Finally, 12 coupled Bayesian coalescent skylines contrast Pleistocene savanna/forest refugia and 19th-20th century maritime timber bridgehead bottlenecks against sharp locus-specific Ne compressions at nuclear GH9 cellulase and hexamerin caste loci relative to neutral mitochondrial COX1/COII (1Ne) and Katoh E-INS-i-aligned ribosomal 16S/28S/ITS rDNA (4Ne) reservoirs. Autonomous 100% Native Rust bio-suite-supervisor synthesis across 544 verified NCBI records (L = 44,075 aligned columns, 32 RuNIE chains, 11.44M quartets, 300k MCMC generations in 238.59 s) resolves the 238.4 Ma-to-present global radiation, GH9 cellulase & CYP4G15 evolution, and 12 regional vs. multi-locus skylines of Isoptera. research.abstract: Abstract Purpose To investigate how artificial intelligence (AI) systems detect referable diabetic retinopathy (DR) from retinal photographs by analysing heatmap patterns and determining their overlap with DR features. Methods Fifty-four AI systems were developed using 27 backbone architectures, with each implemented as both binary-referable and multi-class grading models based on the International Clinical Diabetic Retinopathy (ICDR) grading scale. Models were trained on DDR, BRSET and Kaggle datasets. After training, each model analysed 749 images with DR feature annotations, with Grad-CAM, Integrated Gradients, LIME and SHAP heatmaps generated and compared to pixel-level annotations of microaneurysms, haemorrhages, exudates, cotton wool spots, venous beading, intraretinal microvascular abnormalities and neovascularisation. Results All models achieved acceptable predictive performance (AUROC >0.8 for most architectures). Heatmap analysis revealed consistent attention to the central and temporal macular region. Exudates and cotton wool spots were highlighted most frequently by the heatmaps, with venous beading and neovascularisation at the disc showing poor overall coverage for binary referable classifiers. Models grading per the ICDR scale demonstrated higher coverage for all features. Substantial variability was observed between architectures, suggesting different feature detection capabilities. Interestingly, the heatmap analysis indicated that the models may be using different features to the ICDR grading scale definitions. Conclusion AI models do not uniformly correlate with all DR features when detecting referable DR, limiting their predictive performance in unusual presentations. Heatmap aggregation analysis provides a scalable method for analysing model behaviour, allowing strengths and weaknesses to be assessed. These findings may help improve clinician’s trust and acceptance of AI.

research.journal: Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Medicine
research.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB), represents an important cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide for which an improved vaccine and immunodiagnostics are urgently needed. CD4+ and CD8+ T cells play an important role in host defense to TB. Definition of the immunodominant antigens recognized by these T cells is critical for improved understanding of the immunobiology of TB and for development of vaccines and diagnostics. Herein, we review antigens and epitopes recognized by classically human leukocyte antigen (HLA) class I- and class II-restricted CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in humans infected with MTB, as defined using either targeted or genome-wide approaches. We address the extent to which these antigens have been defined as immunodominant, protective, and/or specific to disease stages in humans and, with particular relevance to CD8+ T-cell recognition, whether these antigens are displayed by MTB-infected cells.

research.abstract: Abstract Mammals have repeatedly evolved specialized diets, including a variety of predatory diets targeting different prey animals. Prior research has found differences in positive selection, gene family evolution, and gene functional loss across diets, but has primarily classified mammals into the three categories of herbivory, carnivory, and omnivory. Here we divide “carnivores” into vertivores and invertivores, due to the differences in nutrient composition of those food sources. We find significant differences in molecular evolutionary rates of multiple genes and gene sets between vertivores and invertivores, with vertivores having lower evolutionary rates of immune related genes, and invertivores having lower evolutionary rates of DNA repair genes and olfactory genes. By comparing evolutionary rates of vertivores, invertivores, and the combination of all carnivores against herbivores, we find that the method of classifying predatory species influences findings of differences between predators and herbivores. Our results in the combined carnivore-herbivore comparison are more similar to those of the invertivore-herbivore comparison than to those of the vertivore-herbivore comparison, which suggests that prior studies on carnivory may have been detecting patterns of molecular evolution related to invertivory. Lineages across all predatory diets have lower evolutionary rates of lipid metabolism genes relative to herbivores, though the specific genes and pathways showing these signatures, particularly those related to steroid hormone metabolism, differ between predatory diets. Taken together, these analyses of molecular evolutionary rates across nuanced predatory diets provide novel insights into the evolution of vertebrate- and invertebrate-based diets, as well as carnivory as a whole. Significance Statement Several studies have used genome-wide gene sequences from mammals with different diets to identify genes with patterns of natural selection related to diet. However, these studies were limited in part due to the common choice to combine invertebrate-based (e.g., insects, shellfish) and vertebrate-based (e.g., fish, birds, other mammals) diets in their analyses. By separating these diets in our study, we identify genes that experienced selection related to these different food sources across mammals, and provide clarification of patterns found by previous studies.

research.abstract: The B3 superfamily is one of the largest plant transcription factor gene families, yet its evolutionary dynamics in dioecious species like Cannabis sativa remain largely unexplored. Here, we present a comprehensive phylogenetic, molecular evolution, and transcriptomic analysis of B3 domain-containing genes in Arabidopsis thaliana , C. sativa , and Humulus lupulus . Using a gene mining pipeline, we identified 110, 101, and 88 B3 genes across the five established subfamilies ( ARF , ABI3 , HSI , RAV , and REM), respectively. We identified two distinct evolutionary trajectories with the B3 superfamily. On the one hand the REM subfamily was by far the largest and characterized by massive lineage-specific tandem duplications subjected to relaxed selective constraint, suggesting distinct or partially redundant roles in reproductive development. On the other hand, specific non-tandem clades remained highly conserved under strong purifying selection. Detailed analysis of the candidate sex-determination gene CsREM16 showed low dN/dS ratios, clear one-to-one orthology across studied species, and unique persistent sex-biased expression across all six analyzed developmental stages in C. sativa . Comparative analysis of its ortholog HlREM16 confirmed a conserved female-biased expression in H. lupulus . Together, these results demonstrate a dual-mode evolutionary dynamic in the B3 superfamily and particularly in the REM genes and establish CsREM16 as a strong candidate for sex determination in C. sativa , with a potentially conserved role in H. lupulus .

research.abstract: Computing phylogenetic likelihoods becomes challenging when the continuous-time Markov chain has a large state space. At each branch, pruning algorithms require terms of the form $e^{Q t}\cdot B$, where $Q$ is an $S \times S$ rate matrix (e.g., for $S$ states), $t$ is a branch length, and the columns of matrix $B$ (e.g., $B \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{S \times L}$) are partial-likelihood vectors for $L$ site patterns. Many implementations calculate the dense transition matrix $P(t)=e^{Q t}$ via eigendecomposition and multiply it by $B$. This strategy is efficient for small state spaces, but it can be inefficient for large sparse rate matrices because forming $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices destroys sparsity and its cost may not be well amortized when $L$ is small. We implement an alternative likelihood kernel based on the Al-Mohy and Higham (2011) algorithm for computing the action of the matrix exponential directly, avoiding explicit construction of $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices. The resulting method takes full advantage of the sparsity of $Q$. We implement this method as a CPU-based extension to the BEAGLE library and evaluate it on two large-state molecular models: a Markov-modulated codon model of heterotachy with $M$ selective regimes and $61\cdot M$ possible states, and a codon-pair model of interlocus gene conversion between two paralogs with $61^2=3\,721$ possible states. Our results characterize when action-based likelihood computation improves performance over calculating $e^{Q t}$ directly. We show that this method enables fast, scalable inference for complex models, removing a key computational barrier to the study of evolution with large state space models.

research.abstract: Purpose Molecular diagnostic tests and sputum-based assays are common techniques for the initial evaluation of tuberculosis (TB). However, given their limitations in certain clinical contexts, efforts have been made to develop other diagnostic markers. This review evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of a three-gene host-response test (TB score) for the diagnosis of TB. Methods We performed systematic searches in seven databases until July 2026. We included observational studies evaluating the diagnostic accuracy of the TB score to diagnosis of TB across different clinical contexts. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Meta-analysis was performed using the logit function, and GRADE was employed to assess certainty of evidence (CoE). Results Twenty-eight studies were included. For distinguishing pulmonary TB from other respiratory diseases, the TB score showed a pooled sensitivity and specificity of 0.80 (95% CI: 0.73-0.84) and 0.72 (95% CI: 0.64-0.78), respectively, with an AUC of 0.82. When comparing pulmonary TB to healthy controls, sensitivity was 0.75 and specificity was 0.86, with an AUC of 0.87. Performance was lower for meningeal tuberculosis (sensitivity 0.58; specificity 0.67) and for distinguishing active from latent TB (sensitivity 0.73; specificity 0.76). Risk of bias was generally low. The CoE for most outcomes was very low. Conclusion The TB score shows moderate diagnostic accuracy for pulmonary TB, with pooled sensitivity below the WHO TPP minimum for a standalone triage test. High heterogeneity and very low CoE limit confidence in these findings. Its potential role as a complementary tool remains investigational and requires validation in prospective studies.

research.abstract: Abstract Mosaic chromosomal alterations (mCAs) have been extensively studied in cancer and clonal hematopoiesis but less so in healthy solid tissues. Here, we characterized mCAs in 19 tissues across 25 donors (aged 42–89+ years) by analyzing >200x whole-genome sequencing data generated by the Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Network. Across 722 tissue samples, we identified 1,008 autosomal mCAs >1 Mb in length and ubiquitous losses of sex chromosomes. Surprisingly, the highest levels of Y chromosome loss in males (5–10% cell fraction in elderly donors) were observed in the lung, adrenal gland, and heart. These tissues also tended to experience more X loss in females, revealing a gradient of mitotic error burden across human tissues. Autosomal aneuploidies displayed distinct tissue-specific patterns indicative of negative selection against most events, except in the adrenal gland, in which low-level aneuploidy was pervasive. In contrast to the adrenal gland, testis rarely harbored aneuploidies but frequently experienced low-level copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity (CN-LOH), suggesting increased mitotic recombination in spermatogonial stem cells. Recurrent X chromosome losses within tissues of female donors exhibited allelic skews explained by a combination of genetic and epigenetic effects. Together, these results show that the chromosomal landscape of aging human tissues is shaped by genetics and recurrent mutations, most but not all of which are held in check by purifying selection.

research.abstract: BACKGROUND: Species inhabiting high-elevation environments face energetic and physiological challenges, creating opportunities for adaptive divergence from lowland taxa. The yellow-tailed woolly monkey (Lagothrix flavicauda), a Critically Endangered primate endemic to high-elevation forests in Andean Perú, provides a unique system for investigating the evolutionary consequences of long-term occupation of high elevations. We used Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT) to generate a high-coverage mitochondrial reference genome using low-quality fecal samples. Using this and a new mitogenome from a closely-related lowland common woolly monkey (L. lagotricha poeppigii), we estimated divergence dates and calculated substitution ratios to investigate the evolutionary history of both Lagothrix taxa and assess whether high-elevation living has left signatures of selection in the mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation genes of L. flavicauda. RESULTS: We assembled a high-coverage (9190X) reference mitogenome of 16,603 bp for L. flavicauda from a 15-year-old fecal sample, and a novel mitogenome for L. lagotricha poeppigii from fresh tissue (112X, 16,590 bp). Our phylogenetic reconstruction is consistent with other platyrrhine primate phylogenies with high bootstrap support, with the two Lagothrix taxa showing evidence of having diverged from one another ~ 2.8 million years ago. Substitution (d N /d S) ratios suggest purifying selection on protein-coding mitogenomic regions in all assessed lineages. CONCLUSIONS: We found no evidence of positive selection acting on mitochondrial protein-coding genes in either L. flavicauda or the broader genus Lagothrix; all analyses instead support pervasive purifying selection across genes involved in oxidative phosphorylation. These results suggest that unlike in some other non-human primates occupying high elevations, the adaptive response of L. flavicauda to living in the Andes does not appear to involve evolution in the mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation pathway, and likely involves alternative genetic pathways or mechanisms not captured by mitochondrial sequence evolution. By providing the first publicly available high-coverage mitochondrial genome for L. flavicauda, this study establishes a foundation for future population mitogenomic investigations of adaptation, evolutionary history, and conservation in this Critically Endangered, high-altitude primate.

research.abstract: BackgroundCardiovascular prevention is increasingly prioritised using burden estimates, yet disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) reward late-stage treatment by construction. Whether that bias is large for cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, and where the population is accumulating relative to where the burden sits, is unknown. MethodsWe pooled nine National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cycles (2005-2023) and assigned CKM stages 0-4 from measured blood pressure, adiposity, glycaemia, lipids, kidney function, urine albumin, self-reported cardiovascular disease, and 10-year PREVENT risk. Years lived with disability used GBD disability weights. Years of life lost combined national death counts, stage-specific mortality from linked mortality files (1999-2018), and period life tables. A second aim attributed burden to smoking and physical inactivity, two exposures outside the CKM definition. ResultsIn 2021-2023, 13.8% of adults were stage 0, 21.3% stage 1, 49.1% stage 2, 6.5% stage 3, and 9.3% stage 4. CKM accounted for 20.0 million DALYs annually (7,881 age-standardised per 100,000), of which 4.1 million were YLD and 15.9 million attributable YLL. Stages 3-4, 15.8% of adults, generated 76% of attributable YLL; stage 4 alone generated 65% of YLD and 49% of attributable YLL. Adjusted mortality rose from stage 2 (hazard ratio 1.39) through stage 4 (3.22), while stage 1 did not differ from stage 0 (0.99; 95% CI, 0.78-1.25). Between 2006 and 2016, stage 0 prevalence fell 2.3% per year and stage 1 rose 3.1% per year. Smoking and physical inactivity accounted for 30.5% of burden (95% CI, 25.7-35.1). ConclusionsCKM burden is concentrated in stages 3-4, where excess mortality begins, while the population has been shifting into stage 1, where mortality is normal. DALY-based prioritisation will therefore systematically underfund the stage in which the next generation of patients is being created. What Is KnownO_LICKM syndrome was defined by the American Heart Association in 2023 and affects most US adults; its burden has so far been expressed only as stage prevalence. C_LIO_LIBurden estimates are used to set prevention priorities, but stage-specific health loss has not been quantified. C_LI What the Study AddsO_LICKM accounts for approximately 20.0 million DALYs per year in US adults; 76% of attributable years of life lost arise in the 15.8% of adults at stages 3-4. C_LIO_LIStage 1 carries no excess mortality after adjustment, yet has expanded by 3.1% per year since 2006, so burden and population growth sit at opposite ends of the syndrome. research.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Tuberculosis contact investigation (TBCI) facilitates early detection of TB among household contacts. However, evidence on the additional contribution of repeat TBCI in high-burden settings remains limited. We assessed the contribution of repeat TBCI at 6 and 12 months to TB case detection in Kasama District, Zambia. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational cohort analysis of routinely collected programme data from five purposively selected high-volume TB diagnostic facilities. Household contacts of bacteriologically confirmed TB patients notified between January 2023 and April 2024 underwent symptom-based TB screening at baseline and at 6 and 12 months. We estimated round-specific TB detection yields, the cumulative proportion diagnosed with TB, and the contribution of repeat investigations to overall case detection. Results Among 1,250 index TB patients, 3,648 household contacts were identified and screened at baseline. TB was diagnosed in 143 (3.9%) contacts at baseline, 31 (0.9%) at month 6, and 25 (0.7%) at month 12. Overall, 199 (5.5%) contacts were diagnosed with TB across the three screening rounds, of whom 159 (79.9%) had bacteriologically confirmed disease. Repeat investigations identified 56 additional cases, representing 28.1% of all TB diagnoses. Conclusions Repeat TBCI at 6 and 12 months identified additional TB cases beyond baseline screening, although detection yields declined across successive rounds. These findings support further evaluation of risk-based follow-up strategies and more sensitive baseline screening approaches to optimize TB case detection and resource utilization in high-burden settings.
